tagline: The small riverside town of Mae Klong, where three waters meet — home to the Maeklong Railway Market, Amphawa Floating Market, and coconut groves everywhere
introHtml:
Samut Songkhram is Thailand's smallest province, and most people just call it Mae Klong, after the main river that runs through town and out to the Gulf. The land around here sits in brackish three-water country, with coconut groves, lychee and pomelo orchards, and salt pans along the coast.

It's a little over an hour's drive from Bangkok. Most people come to walk the Maeklong Railway Market, where the train runs straight through the stalls, take an evening boat to watch the fireflies at Amphawa, and stay a night at a homestay by the canal — then wake up early to give alms to monks rowing past.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable with little rain, good for boat trips and floating markets. The rainy season is actually when the fireflies show up best.

highlights.name: Maeklong Railway Market (Talad Rom Hub)
highlights.blurb: A fresh market where stalls are set up right over the railway tracks. When a train is coming, the vendors fold back their awnings and pull their goods aside to let it pass, then set everything up again — a sight people come specifically to see.

highlights.name: Amphawa Floating Market
highlights.blurb: A floating market along Amphawa Canal that buzzes on Friday to Sunday evenings, with food sold from boats. You eat your way along the waterside walkway, then hop on a boat to watch the fireflies after dark.

highlights.name: King Rama II Park and Bang Kung Camp
highlights.blurb: Amphawa is the birthplace of King Rama II, with a memorial park to stroll through. Nearby at Bang Kung Camp is the Bodhi-wrapped chapel, where tree roots cover the entire building.

highlights.name: Mae Klong coconut groves and coconut sugar
highlights.blurb: The whole province is full of coconut groves, with open-air stoves boiling down fresh coconut sugar that you can stop to watch and buy. It's one of Mae Klong's signature products.

highlights.name: Don Hoi Lot
highlights.blurb: A sandbar at the mouth of the Mae Klong River where razor clams burrow into the mud. At low tide you can walk out and dig for them, and there's a long row of seafood restaurants along the shore.

highlights.name: Wat Bang Kung and Wat Bang Khae Noi, by the Mae Klong River
highlights.blurb: Several old riverside temples you can visit in a single day by boat or car, with carved teak chapels and a Buddha image set within a Bodhi tree.

foodScene.name: Mae Klong and Don Hoi Lot seafood
foodScene.note: The mouth of the Mae Klong River brings in fresh shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish every day. Restaurants out at Don Hoi Lot do stir-fried razor clams with chili and grilled prawns right by the sea.

foodScene.name: Razor clams (hoi lot)
foodScene.note: The province's signature catch — stir-fried with chili and herbs, in chu chee curry, or simply blanched with a dip. The meat is uniquely sweet, and you'll find it around Don Hoi Lot.

foodScene.name: Mae Klong mackerel (pla tu)
foodScene.note: The short, plump bent-neck mackerel from Mae Klong Bay, steamed in little baskets and sold at the markets. Fried and eaten with shrimp-paste chili dip, it's a humble local meal.

foodScene.name: Food at Amphawa Floating Market
foodScene.note: In the evening there's boat noodles, fried oyster omelet, grilled prawns, and other grilled bites sold from boats along the canal. You can graze your way through the whole evening.

foodScene.name: Coconut sugar and Mae Klong sweets
foodScene.note: Fresh coconut sugar boiled down from the groves goes into all sorts of desserts — thong yot, sticky rice with coconut, and sweets made with palm-sugar cakes.

foodScene.name: Mae Klong pomelo and lychee
foodScene.note: The brackish-water orchards here grow big white pomelos and local kom lychees, in season for buying straight from the roadside groves.

foodScene.name: Canalside and riverside cafes
foodScene.note: Around Amphawa and along the canals you'll find cafes in wooden houses and coffee shops by the water, easy places to sip a coffee and watch the boats go by.

foodScene.name: Noodles and snacks at Mae Klong market
foodScene.note: The railway market and the in-town markets have noodles, rice-and-curry plates, and snacks to eat while you wait for the train.

attractions.name: Maeklong Railway Market
attractions.blurb: A fresh market straddling the railway tracks, where vendors fold their awnings and pull goods aside to let the train through — the defining image of Mae Klong.

attractions.name: Amphawa Floating Market
attractions.blurb: A canalside floating market that buzzes on Friday–Sunday evenings, with food from boats and a pier for firefly cruises.

attractions.name: King Rama II Memorial Park
attractions.blurb: A park and museum in the birthplace of King Rama II beside Amphawa Canal, with Thai houses and gardens to wander through.

attractions.name: Bang Kung Camp (Bodhi-wrapped chapel)
attractions.blurb: An old chapel within a Thonburi-era army camp, its entire structure wrapped in the roots of a Bodhi tree.

attractions.name: Don Hoi Lot
attractions.blurb: A muddy sandbar at the mouth of the Mae Klong River where you can dig for razor clams at low tide, with seafood restaurants along the shore.

attractions.name: Amphawa firefly boat cruise
attractions.blurb: An evening boat trip along the canals to watch fireflies flicker in the lamphu trees by the water, best in the rainy season.

attractions.name: Wat Bang Kung and the Mae Klong River temples
attractions.blurb: Several old riverside temples you can visit along one route by car or boat.

attractions.name: Coconut groves and sugar stoves
attractions.blurb: Stop by a coconut grove to watch fresh coconut sugar being boiled down, taste it and buy some — a rural canalside scene.
